Internship prep.Beginner: An interviewer asks: what is a data pipeline, and what could break in it when the database structure changes in a new release?
Internship prep.Experienced: An interviewer asks: how do you make a pipeline safe to re-run, so that a retry or rollback never duplicates or loses data?

Keep up with trends.Beginner: Many teams now process data as a live stream instead of in nightly batches. What is the difference, and why does it matter when a release breaks something?
Keep up with trends.Experienced: Data contracts are a growing practice. How would an agreed contract between the app team and your pipeline have caught this change before it shipped?

Use AI effectively.Beginner: If an AI assistant told you to patch the live system, what would you want to check before trusting it?
Use AI effectively.Experienced: An AI agent proposes a hot patch with a clean diff. What evidence would you require before it touches production, and who owns that decision?

Internship prep.Beginner: An interviewer asks: what are three simple checks you would run on a new dataset to see whether it can be trusted?
Internship prep.Experienced: An interviewer asks: how would you validate a backfill before it overwrites production tables, and how would you undo it if it went wrong?

Keep up with trends.Beginner: Teams now watch data the way they watch servers (data observability). What would you monitor to know the data is fresh and complete?
Keep up with trends.Experienced: How would automated freshness, volume and schema alerts have caught this before the ops manager did, and which would you set up first?

Use AI effectively.Beginner: An AI suggests a quick fix for the bad readings. How could you check it worked without trusting it blindly?
Use AI effectively.Experienced: The AI's fix passes its own tests. How do you build an independent check, and what would its tests not catch?

Internship prep.Beginner: An interviewer asks: what is personal data, and why shouldn't it appear in logs shared with the whole team?
Internship prep.Experienced: An interviewer asks: how would you design logging so personal data never appears, instead of masking it afterwards?

Keep up with trends.Beginner: Many companies now mask personal data by default, and laws like Kenya's Data Protection Act push them to. What does 'by default' change about how you build a pipeline?
Keep up with trends.Experienced: Compare masking, tokenizing and dropping fields at ingestion. What does each cost you when debugging?

Use AI effectively.Beginner: If you paste these logs into an AI assistant, where might the data go, and what should you remove first?
Use AI effectively.Experienced: Your team wants an LLM for incident triage. What data boundary would you set, and how would you enforce it in the pipeline?
